messages:
acme_infra: Hey team — starting ~09:10UTC we saw a sharp increase in 500s and 401s for requests originating in EU customers. Latency jumped from ~60ms to 1.2s and some calls failed with 401. Impacting multiple tenants. Can you triage?

shawn_support: Thanks, sorry for the hit. Can you paste a sample request id + region header? Any recent config changes on your side?

acme_infra: sample request-id: req_0a9f3c. We don't set region header explicitly. We hit the standard /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Attaching a snippet of the failing curl:

acme_infra: ```curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions```

acme_infra: Response for that req: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized {"error":"token scope mismatch for region: us-east-1"} and latency header: x-rlatency:1200ms, x-rregion: us-east-1

shawn_support: Huh, token scope mismatch for us-east-1. Did the request route cross-region? Nina, can you check routing logs for req_0a9f3c?

nina_sre: Looking now. autoscaler-bot flagged hotshard on eu-west-1 at 09:08UTC (98% GPU). Routing policy: auto-spillover -> fallback to nearest available region (us-east-1). I'm seeing the traffic diverted at the router layer; requests kept the EU token, which is scope-limited. That explains the 401s.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] 2025-10-02T09:08:14Z eu-west-1 pool:hot_shard=98% queued=420 spillover=enabled

eli_engineer: The router should rewrite tokens only for cross-region migrations when using dedicated capacity mapping. For hosted customers tokens are region-scoped. We had a recent change to aggressive spillover thresholds to avoid timeouts; looks like it triggered earlier than intended during a burst.

maria_ops: Customer reports billing spiked too. If requests are now served from us-east we may be billing at different rate tier. Need to confirm whether billing metering used original region or actual serving region.

shawn_support: Ok action items: (1) stop further automatic cross-region spillover for this account (temp pin), (2) re-run affected requests or advise customer about reissuing scoped tokens, (3) confirm billing treatment. Nina can you apply a pin?

nina_sre: Applied a manual region pin (eu-west-1) for acme org at 09:20UTC. Also lowered spillover threshold from 95% to 99% for eu pools to reduce premature migration.

eli_engineer: Quick repro steps for devs: run 500 small concurrent chat requests from an EU IP to trigger queueing. If pool saturates, router will select fallback region. Observe headers: x-rregion shows fallback region, x-auth-scope remains eu-west -> leads to 401. Example load script:

eli_engineer: ```for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions & done; wait```

acme_infra: Thanks. For mitigation we rotated the token but that was a pain. Is there a plan to have router attach a short-lived passthrough token when doing spillover? That would avoid customer reauth.

eli_engineer: Roadmap note: we discussed token-minting proxy for spillover during emergency fallbacks. Needs KMS onboarding and extra audit controls. Not trivial but a known gap. Logging ticket: INC-2025-4423 created.

maria_ops: Billing thread: engineering, please confirm whether served-region or originating-region is used for metering. If served-region, we should calculate customer credits for unintended cross-region execution.

nina_sre: Metering system currently records serving node region. I triggered a quick report for the acme org for the 09:05-09:30 window. Preliminary: ~18k tokens charged at us-east rates.

acme_infra: We need a credit and a postmortem. Also can you add an explicit client-side header to allow region pin in the API? We can set X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1.

shawn_support: Good suggestion. Short term: we've pinned you and issued a credit hold. I'll follow up with billing. Long term: engineering to evaluate passthrough token + opt-in client header.

eli_engineer: Follow-up: added a quick guard in the router to reject cross-region routing when auth scope mismatch detected (returns 409 with message instructing to reissue token or pin region) — deployed a hotfix at 09:42UTC. This prevents silent 401s and weird billing.

acme_infra: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Can you share the postmortem timeline when ready?

nina_sre: Will produce a short incident doc. Root cause: capacity exhaustion + aggressive auto-spillover + region-scoped tokens led to auth failures and cross-region billing. Remediation: pin, threshold tweak, router guard. Next steps: design token-minting proxy and add explicit client header.

shawn_support: Closing loop: acme, I've placed a billing credit request and escalated for postmortem. Please open a ticket if you see any remaining 4xx/5xx. :thumbsup:

acme_infra: :thumbsup: thanks everyone, will monitor and report if anything else pops up.
